must_remember: The moment of inertia of a thin hollow cylinder (shell) about its longitudinal geometric axis is $I = MR^2$.
The moment of inertia of a solid cylinder about its longitudinal geometric axis is $I = \frac{1}{2}MR^2$.
Both solid and hollow cylinder longitudinal moments of inertia are completely independent of their length $L$.
The moment of inertia of a solid cylinder about a transverse axis through its centre of mass is $I = \frac{1}{4}MR^2 + \frac{1}{12}ML^2$.
Using the parallel axis theorem, the moment of inertia of a solid cylinder about a tangential longitudinal axis is $I = \frac{3}{2}MR^2$.

glossary.meaning: A quantity expressing a body's tendency to resist angular acceleration, dependent on mass distribution relative to the axis of rotation.
The central geometric axis running along the length of the cylinder.
An axis perpendicular to the length of the cylinder.
A cylindrical shell characterized by both an inner radius $R_1$ and an outer radius $R_2$.
